node-2.label: The patient occasionally drank alcohol and had no history of viral hepatitis, steatohepatitis, autoimmune liver disease, or metabolic liver disease

node-4.label: After stopping alcohol and axitinib, her hepatobiliary enzyme levels remained unchanged

why.why: Expert pathology and radiology analyses both conclude drug injury is unlikely. The cholestatic pattern, hilar enhancing lesion, MRI hypointensity, and biopsy-proven PAX8-positive malignant cells occluding interlobular veins and destroying bile ducts point to malignant biliary obstruction. Lack of improvement after stopping alcohol and axitinib further argues against drug-induced injury, lowering confidence from 0.08 to 0.04.

Expert consensus supports a structural malignant biliary obstruction: cholestatic ALP/GGT elevation, irregular enhancing hilar lesion, MRI hypointense hepatic parenchyma, and biopsy-proven PAX8-positive malignant cells occluding veins and destroying bile ducts. Lack of response to stopping alcohol and axitinib reinforces a non-drug obstructive process, raising confidence from 0.85 to 0.92.

Biopsy shows PAX8-positive malignant cells with interlobular vein occlusion and bile duct destruction, and all expert analyses favor malignant biliary obstruction. Common hepatocellular causes were already excluded, making occult hepatocellular disease very unlikely and reducing confidence from 0.03 to 0.02.

node-16.label: Malignant biliary obstruction due to metastatic carcinoma of Müllerian/gynecologic origin (ovarian or endometrial)
